$comment: The part of the energy system the dashboard doesn't draw but the OSeMOSYS model needs: timeslices, capacity and demand profiles, fuel imports, the end-use technologies behind each demand sector and the system parameters. With the scenarios (src/data/scenarios) this is the whole model input; backend/energy_model/osemosys/build.py turns them into a tz-osemosys model. Base SI units: energy J, power W, money $ (real), mass kg, fractions. ALL VALUES ARE SAMPLE DATA (order-of-magnitude public figures: IEA WEO / NREL ATB / Lazard ranges); replace with sourced data before relying on the results. Known caveats: power-source emission factors are lifecycle (IPCC AR5 medians) while end-use fuels and gas use combustion factors, so the CO2 total mixes the two bases; electricity-import capex (an interconnector) and deep-geothermal capex are at the optimistic end; blue hydrogen's factor assumes partial capture.
$reserveMarginComment: Firm capacity (W × each source's capacityCredit) must cover the highest timeslice electricity load × this factor. The timeslices are averages (the highest is only ~1.3× the yearly mean, while the hourly peak is ~1.65–2× it), so the factor holds both the peak-to-timeslice ratio (~1.25) and a 15% planning reserve: 1.25 × 1.15 ≈ 1.45.

timeslices.$comment: Share of the year in each timeslice (sums to 1).

capacityProfiles.$comment: Shape of a source's output over the timeslices; multiplied by the source's capacityFactor after scaling to a year-weighted mean of 1. A source without `profile` is dispatchable: it may run up to `dispatchableAvailability` in every timeslice.

demandProfiles.$comment: Shape of a demand kind over the timeslices (scaled to a year-weighted mean of 1). Kinds without an entry follow the year split (flat).

fuelImports.$comment: free fuel, so capped at the available resource: ~6 Mt/y of municipal waste × ~10 GJ/t ≈ 60 PJ/y (J/y)

fuelBlends.$comment: What can supply the `Fuels` carrier of the end-use technologies, with its combustion emissions (kg CO2eq per J of fuel); same factors as FINAL_EMISSION_FACTOR in model/fuel.ts.

endUse.$comment: Per sector kind: the technologies that turn a carrier into the sector's demand. `efficiency` is useful output per J of the carrier, relative to the electric technology (transport: 1 TWh of electricity replaces 2.5 TWh of fuel, the dashboard's electrifyOffset). The demand commodity is in useful energy: the dashboard's electricity, fuels and gas of the sector, each × its efficiency. capitalCost / fixedCost are per W of useful-output capacity; capacityFactor is its average yearly use (it sizes the base-year fleet; in any one timeslice the fleet may run at full capacity). In a `fixed` kind every carrier is held at the dashboard's value (no switching); in the others the model chooses the mix, starting from the base-year fleet, which retires linearly over operatingLife.

fuels.$comment: oil / LPG boilers vs a COP-3 heat pump

electricity.$comment: battery-electric vehicles: ~$32k per car for ~250 W of average useful output

fuels.$comment: combustion vehicles (~$30k per car) (diesel / gasoline / clean fuels / hydrogen through the Fuels blend)
